findings.issue: C4 GMAIL SCOPE (OQ3) asserts 'incoming replies keep using the reply-by-email domain pattern, so we never read the user's Gmail.' This misrepresents the code on disk: the ask/reply loop READS the user's own Gmail inbox today. mail-gog.js listInbox runs `gmail search newer_than:2d` and ask.js explicitly READs inbound replies ('READ replies (EMAIL users only ...)') to capture event locations. There is NO reply-by-email domain-pattern mechanism on disk for the location-reply read; the spec describes 'keep using' a mechanism that does not exist.
findings.evidence: apps/life-call/lib/transport/mail-gog.js:31-37 (listInbox -> `gmail search newer_than:2d`, shaped for the ask.js reply loop); apps/life-call/lib/ask.js:6-8 ('READ: Gemini reads inbound replies'), :247 ('READ replies (EMAIL users only — Telegram replies arrive via the webhook, not here)'); mail-unipile.js:23-24 ('Recent inbox messages (for reading location replies)'). No 'reply-by-email domain' inbound path exists in apps/life-call.
findings.fix: State the truth: today Gmail is READ for location replies. Either (a) spec the reply-by-email inbound domain pipeline as a NEW build (Resend-inbound webhook -> match to pending event) with its own contract + proof, or (b) accept a read scope for Gmail (and address the CASA/RESTRICTED consequence you were avoiding). Do not describe an unbuilt mechanism as an existing 'keep using' pattern.

findings.issue: gmail.send-only scope for Pipedream Gmail users leaves the location-reply READ path unhandled = a functional regression for the connect cohort. The ask loop's location-collection feature depends on reading the user's inbox (listInbox). A Pipedream user granted only gmail.send cannot have their inbox read, so their emailed location replies are never ingested, silently breaking calendar-location backfill for exactly the new-onboarding cohort C4 is meant to enable. C4's 'Dual-read = selector + calendar-read handle both providers' covers CALENDAR read only, not GMAIL reply read.
findings.evidence: apps/life-call/lib/ask.js:208-247 (ask loop sends via mail.send then READs replies via listInbox); mail-gog.js:32-37 (listInbox = gmail search). C4 (spec line 73-78) grants only Calendar + gmail.send and dual-reads only calendar_provider; no gmail-read adapter or reply-by-email fallback is specified for Pipedream users.
findings.fix: Add an EDGE + migration to C4: for send-only users, either route inbound location replies through the (to-be-built) reply-by-email inbound domain, or fall back to Telegram-only location capture, and assert in a test that a Pipedream user's location reply is ingested with zero gmail.readonly scope. Otherwise mark location-reply capture as EMAIL/Composio-only and downgrade the Goal-4 claim ('backend reads calendar + sends mail').

findings.issue: F4 is only partially closed. C4 MIGRATION widens ONLY the sweep selector (scheduler.js:42). If only line 42 is widened, a Pipedream user selected in the sweep is re-filtered OUT the moment the per-user function refetches them, so they still get zero wakes/travel/ask. iteration-1 F4 explicitly cited BOTH scheduler.js:42 AND the getUserByUid site; the iter-2 spec dropped the second one.

findings.issue: F11(c) unresolved: the money-path monitor's Stripe-link extraction is internally contradictory and unpinned. C5 CHECK(b) says 'the /lm?tg=x bundle's Stripe link == registry (bare /lm has none)'. But /lm is `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` (static export) and the ?tg= gate is a CLIENT useEffect — so the SAME static HTML + SAME JS chunk is served for both /lm and /lm?tg=x. STRIPE_LM_URL is inlined into that shared chunk (LmClient is imported at module top), so at the BUNDLE level 'bare /lm has none' is FALSE (both contain it) and the /lm vs /lm?tg=x distinction is meaningless. At the RENDERED-DOM level the Stripe anchor only renders at the 'pay' step, reached only after client-side Google-OAuth + name + phone — which a black-box GHA monitor cannot drive headlessly. Neither extraction method is specified, and the two the spec conflates cannot both be true.
findings.evidence: apps/landing/app/lm/page.tsx:10 (force-static); LmBody.tsx (lipsync-monk worktree):22-41 (tg gate is a client useEffect; standalone -> coming-soon, tg -> LmClient); LmClient.tsx:34 (STRIPE_LM_URL inlined) + :442-448 (anchor rendered only inside the step==='pay' Shell). Spec line 82 CHECK(b) + Goal 5 line 41.
findings.fix: Pin ONE extraction method: fetch the built static chunk(s) under /_next/static and grep for the Stripe URL (then drop the false '/lm?tg=x vs bare /lm' distinction — the chunk is shared), OR add a dedicated SSR/edge endpoint that emits the effective Stripe link. Then the content assertion (c) fetches that Stripe URL directly. Remove the 'bare /lm has none' premise.

findings.issue: The 'verified on disk' fact — bare /lm = coming-soon gate; LmClient renders only on ?tg= (LmBody.tsx:41-63) — is true in ONLY ONE of three on-disk worktrees. In .claude/worktrees/lipsync-monk the gate exists (LmBody.tsx has the tg useEffect + coming-soon at lines ~22-63, matching the cited range). In .claude/worktrees/agent-a6417f77d0f47a1cc and agent-a0389b9e243c82be2 LmBody.tsx is 38 lines and renders <LmClient/> UNCONDITIONALLY with no gate and no ?tg= branch. The spec does not state which branch/worktree is authoritative, so the invariant the monitor depends on (Goal 5 / C5) is not uniformly true on disk.
findings.evidence: lipsync-monk/apps/landing/app/lm/LmBody.tsx:22-63 (gate present); agent-a6417f77d0f47a1cc/apps/landing/app/lm/LmBody.tsx:1-38 and agent-a0389b9e243c82be2/.../LmBody.tsx:1-38 (unconditional <LmClient/>, no gate). Spec §2 line 27 cites LmBody.tsx:41-63.
findings.fix: Pin the authoritative branch/commit for apps/landing in §0/§2 and confirm the gate exists there; a monitor built against a gate that only exists in one worktree will misfire once a different tree is deployed.

findings.issue: The 'verified external facts' table understates the wake schedule: it says 'Wake = T-10 firm + T-5 harsh | scheduler.js:30-33'. The cited code defines THREE levels including T-15 gentle. A spec whose own evidence table drops a wake level risks C1 impl reasoning about which wakes carry the one-way clip vs escalation being built on an incomplete model.
findings.evidence: apps/life-call/scheduler.js:29-33 WAKE_LEVELS = [{min:15,gentle},{min:10,firm},{min:5,harsh}]; spec line 22 lists only T-10 + T-5.
findings.fix: Correct the fact to T-15 gentle + T-10 firm + T-5 harsh, and state whether the one-way clip fires on all three levels.

findings.issue: C2's deterministic JP gate requires each endpoint's lat/lon ('both endpoints' geo fall in a JP bounding box') but the system's inputs are free-text address strings (lm_users.home_address, gcal event location — today passed to Google as {address: src}). The spec does not specify how an address becomes geo without a paid Google Geocoding call, re-introducing per-route Google cost into a COST-REDUCTION feature. The stated gate is also circular: 'geo in JP box AND resolve in the feed (via places/suggest probe)' — the geo is produced BY the suggest call, so the bounding-box test cannot precede feed-resolution as written.
findings.evidence: apps/life-call/lib/travel.js:73-77 buildDriveBody({address:src}) and :106-124 legacyTransitMinutes use address strings, never lat/lon; the transit fixtures take geo coords as input (from.id='geo:35.681,139.767'). Spec line 61 asserts a geo-bounds gate with no address->geo step.
findings.fix: Specify the address->geo step and prove it is free (e.g. transit.ls8h.com places/suggest returns geo, used both to resolve AND to bound-check), or state the Google Geocoding cost and cap it. Define the ordering: probe places/suggest FIRST, derive geo, THEN apply the JP bounding box + feed-resolvability.
